subtype: Approach: share personal data freely with the chatbot [Pitfall]
passage:
Damini: I pasted my bank statements into the chatbot to work out where my money goes
Karthik: All of them?
Damini: And some of Meera's messages, she'd sent me a long voice-note transcript about her family. I wanted advice on what to say back
Karthik: Did Meera say you could?
Damini: No.
Karthik: Damini, that text may be stored somewhere. And it's her private stuff, she never agreed
Damini: I didn't think. It just felt like talking to a friend
Karthik: It isn't one. It's a service. Delete the chat, and you should tell Meera what you did
Damini: She'll be so hurt. I'll tell her tonight

qa.q: Whose messages did Damini paste, besides the bank statements?
What is Damini feeling when Damini says Meera will be so hurt?
qa.a: Damini feels guilty and worried, realising that a private message was shared without permission.

qa.q: What could Damini do next to repair the situation, and why?
qa.a: Damini could delete the chat, tell Meera honestly and ask before using anyone's words again, because trust depends on the friend hearing it from Damini first.

qa.q: How might Meera feel on learning the messages were pasted into a chatbot?
qa.a: Meera may feel hurt or exposed, since the family details were shared with a service without any chance to say no.

grounding: The person pastes bank statements and a friend's private messages into a chatbot, compromising privacy without the friend's agreement.
